name: Abawiri
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 further work by the same author (or citing it for stress) agrees.
catalog_citation: Yoder, Brendon E. 2020. A grammar of Abawiri, a Lakes Plain language of Papua, Indonesia. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara.https://escholarship.org/uc/item/4mj571tr
catalog_quote: Like all other Lakes Plain languages, Abawiri is tonal (§2.4). There are two tone heights, /H/ and /L/, in addition to a derived /M/ tone, that combine to form eight tone patterns on morphemes. Anticipatory tonal polarity before a /L/ tone is a robust phonological process in the language. Prosodic properties of Abawiri intonation units (IUs) are discussed in §2.5 ... [p. 65] Like all Lakes Plain languages for which phonological information is available, Abawiri is a tonal language, that is, “an indication of pitch enters into the lexical realisation of at least some morphemes” (Hyman 2006: 229). ... [p. 67] In Abawiri there are two tones, /H/ and /L/, as well as a derived /M/ tone that only occurs as a result of /H/ tone lowering after a floating /L/ tone. These tones combine into eight tone patterns on nouns (toneless, /L/, /H/, /LH/, /HL/, / LH/, /LHL/, and /ØHL/) and six on verbs ...…

tone_statements.citation: Yoder, Brendon E. 2020. A grammar of Abawiri, a Lakes Plain language of Papua, Indonesia. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara.https://escholarship.org/uc/item/4mj571tr
tone_statements.quote: In Sikaritai there are two level tones, /L/ and /H/, as well as both falling and rising tones (Liem 2007). Doutai has these same four tones; they combine into three tone patterns on monosyllabic nouns and ten patterns on disyllabic nouns (Donohue et al. 2006).
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2.4 'Tone', p.66, paragraph beginning 'There are basic descriptions of at least seven other Lakes Plain tone systems.'
tone_statements.n_tones: 4 (two level /L/ /H/ + falling + rising), attributed to Liem 2007

audit.reasoning: The classification 'tonal' (no word stress described) rests on the 2020 UCSB reference grammar by the sole describer of the language, which we hold as PDF+text; every segment of the deciding quotation and the domain quotation is present verbatim at the stated pages (34, 65, 67; abstract). The negative half of the the primary-stress rule is also checkable: 'stress' never occurs in the 600-page grammar and §2.5 treats only IU-level boundary tones. Glottolog lists no competing description; the one other phonology item (Yoder 2018, Language) is an earlier version of the same tone analysis, explicitly revised in the grammar, and its abstract (downloaded) agrees. Nothing better exists to hold; no reclassification or re-read indicated.

tone.says: Second-hand for Sikaritai (read full text): sec. 2.4 p.66, in a survey of seven Lakes Plain tone systems, states that Sikaritai has two level tones /L/ and /H/ plus falling and rising tones, citing Liem 2007 -- a four-term inventory that differs from Martin 1991's two tonemes with contours analysed as vowel sequences (our statement listed here); p.13 describes Liem 2007 as 'an update' of Martin 1991's phonology sketch and says all these Lakes Plain languages are tonal. No statement on Sikaritai…

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.quote: Abstract: 'Two level tones (/L/ and /H/) combine into eight tone melodies on nouns ... and five on verbs ... The default pitch of tonelessness is L. Several phonological processes involve tone. /H/ is lowered to M tone after a floating /L/. A polar (H) is linked to the final syllable of a non-/H/ word previous to an /L/-toned word. Utterance-final boundary tone L% is linked to all utterance-final syllables. /H/ spreads to the end of nouns but does not spread on verbs.' No mention of stress or accent.
sources.note: Only other phonological publication on Abawiri; per the grammar (p. 67) it carries 'more phonetic details pertaining to the basic tonal analysis' — would let the record cite a peer-reviewed instrumental treatment alongside the dissertation, though the grammar's §2.4 revises and supersedes it and its abstract already matches our classification.
